Habitat description. The type locality, Río Amacuzac at Huajintlán, is in the southwestern area of the Mexican state of Morelos at an elevation of 931 meters. The first author visited the type locality (L- 1989) three decades after the type specimens were collected; unfortunately, no more specimens of A. morelosensis were found, only numerous specimens of A. hydor La Rivers. At the time, the river at the type locality was approximately 40 meters wide and shallow, exposing boulders and cobble (Fig. 6). Distribution. Ambrysus morelosensis is known from only two localities, one in the state of Michoacán and the other in Morelos, in central-western and central Mexico, respectively (Fig. 7). Both localities are at elevations below 1,000 meters and within the limits of the Balsas Basin biogeographical province; more specifically, in the middle (Morelos) and lower (Michoacán) sections of the basin.
